headline: Integrated omics and network filters narrow disease genes to candidate causal targets
label: Integrative Multiomics Target Prioritization
summary: Public multiomic and single-cell datasets now yield causal and network-based target nominations faster than experimental validation can test them.
synthesis: The dominant thread is prioritization of candidate genes, proteins, or lipids by integrating transcriptomic, proteomic, lipidomic, or genetic evidence with network, Mendelian randomization, or machine-learning filters. Several items assign candidates to specific cell types using single-cell resolution, including CSF1R-dependent immunometabolic communication in osteoarthritis, RGL2 across postoperative delirium and Alzheimer's disease, and alveolar macrophage communication in sepsis-induced lung injury analyzed with MEBOCOST. Newer elements include an LLM-agent framework that compares protein co-abundance networks across 820 tissue pairs, yielding 1,833 conserved clusters, and topology-driven proteome integration in engineered heart tissue contrasting epinephrine and doxorubicin. Experimental validation is explicitly reported for ACSL4 in pulmonary hypertension and for the engineered heart tissue contrast, while many other nominations rest on computational or cohort-based evidence.
